h1: Neo Museum — Education & Community Landing Page Design
tagline: Landing page reference built around “Step into the natural world and discover the stories written millions of years ago”, with the layout, timings and palette written down in the brief.
summary: Landing page reference for an education or community brand — 2800ms transitions, Inter, a stats row and cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) easing.
about: Neo Museum is a working reference for an education or community brand: the landing page laid out, measured and ready to rebuild. The page's own headline reads “Step into the natural world and discover the stories written millions of years ago”, and the composition is built around those exact words. The colour scheme is white #FCFCFC underneath and black #0A0A0A for the type, and the page is set in Inter. The reference is built with React and Tailwind CSS, and the layout decisions are stated independently of it. Motion comes down to 2800ms transitions and cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1). It is most useful when the Education & Community landing page has to survive a copy change without a redesign.

layout.title: Top row, one action
layout.body: A short run of links and a single action sit over the landing page, held at type from 12px to 15px and 75vh sections so the bar never competes with the composition behind it. The bar sits over the 640x468 composition without a background of its own, so the media runs edge to edge underneath it.

layout.title: Figures as typography
layout.body: A compact stats strip carries the claims that would otherwise need a paragraph, which keeps the landing page from turning into a feature list. The row is aligned to the same margin as the headline above it.

layout.title: Badge above the fold
layout.body: One badge, one message: the pill sits above the headline in Inter at the smallest step, and nothing else competes for that slot. The pill sits at the smallest step in the brief, so it reads as a label rather than as a second title. Keep it above the headline, never beside it.

layout.title: Top row: wordmark, links, one action
layout.body: Give the wordmark no more room than its type needs. The reference was captured at 640x468.

motion.title: One duration for the controls
motion.body: State changes are specified at 2800ms, so the feedback on the controls is a designed value rather than a browser default. The quoted timing covers state changes, so the feedback is the part of the motion that is specified.

motion.title: The stat counts on entry
motion.body: Figures count up as they enter the viewport, set in Inter at the display size. The count is short enough to read as a reveal rather than as a loading state.

notes: The type is set in Inter on a 12–15px scale, and the spacing follows the same steps.
The display line is Inter at the top of a 12–15px scale, with the interface text on the same face.
Transitions are specified at 2800ms, short enough that the page never feels like it is waiting for an animation.

editorial.title: How the landing page reflows
editorial.body: When the copy is long, the narrow layout breaks first. Here a clamp between 12px and 15px absorbs the change, and the section is held at 75vh and the navigation collapses into a mobile menu. Width changes the measurements, not the reading path.

editorial.title: The argument this landing page makes
editorial.body: There is one promise on this page, and type from 12px to 15px and 75vh sections hold it in place. The page says it out loud: “Step into the natural world and discover the stories written millions of years ago”. Nothing below the fold is asked to carry the offer as well. Neo Museum states the offer once and lets the composition repeat it rather than adding a second claim.

editorial.title: The order behind the landing page
editorial.body: Read the first screen in one pass and the offer is already clear. navigation, the headline, the announcement badge, the stats row and the background clip arrive in sequence, separated by type from 12px to 15px and 75vh sections rather than by decorative dividers. A education reader gets the offer before the options.

faq.question: Is the Neo Museum prompt a finished spec or a starting point?
faq.answer: The captured brief runs 15,036 characters and covers the frame, the type scale, the palette and the transitions. Copying it gives you that text, and sending it to Studio stages the same request with the page already described.

faq.question: What can I do with the Neo Museum brief once I have it?
faq.answer: Everything quoted on the page comes from the captured 15,036-character brief rather than from a description written afterwards. That is why the numbers and the prose agree.

faq.question: Why does the entry name React and Tailwind CSS at all?
faq.answer: Neo Museum was built in React and Tailwind CSS, and the entry says so for provenance. The brief describes positions, sizes and timings, so it rebuilds in any framework that can set type and place elements.

audience: Quote a 640x468 frame in the handoff note so the next build does not have to re-derive it from the page.
If the motion has to be dropped, the landing page still reads, with type from 12px to 15px and 75vh sections doing the hierarchy work.
Made for a solo founder shipping one landing page for an education or community brand and no design system behind them.
